19.reasoning: P and Q are on the main wire with the cell, so they take the parts that go in series: the ammeter (2) and the key (4). R and S are two branches between the same two points, so whatever sits there is in parallel: the resistor (1) and the voltmeter (3), which must be connected across the resistor. Options A and C put the voltmeter in series on the main wire, which is wrong. MSTA's key gives (B), with the voltmeter at R and the resistor at S; option D only swaps the two parallel branches.

12.value: P heat energy, Q kinetic energy, R mechanical energy, S electrical energy
12.reasoning: This is the chain in a steam power plant. The steam in the boiler P carries heat energy; the jet of steam at Q is moving, so it has kinetic energy; it turns the turbine R, giving mechanical energy; and the generator turns that into electrical energy, which reaches the bulb at S. That is option D.

57.value: The wrong pair is HID lamp and krypton-82
57.reasoning: Phosphorus-32 is used to treat polycythemia and radium-223 to treat cancer that has spread to bone, so those pairs are right. High intensity discharge (HID) lamps use krypton-85, not krypton-82, so pair D is wrong. Note that pair C is not right either: cobalt-60 is used to treat cancer, while tumours are usually detected with other isotopes such as arsenic-74.
